correctness.rationale: Read pinned RESULT.md and exact-rational verify_exact.py. For n=3,4,5 every proper centered ball is radius zero or (n>=4) radius one. For each t above weighted global mean q, a vertex new to the maximal high-level set must be adjacent to an input-high vertex, so on a cycle connected components and edge boundary do not increase. For t below q, maximal high-level is the whole cycle, while for min(h)<t<q the input-high set is proper nonempty with boundary≥2. Finite graph coarea integration proves Var(M_w f)≤Var(|f|)-2(q-min|f|). The degree-two inequality W(q-min|f|)≥(w_min/2)Var(|f|) gives sharp norm 1-w_min/W, and a minimum-mass vertex spike realizes equality; uniform weights uniquely minimize this over the mass simplex. Independent exact rational tests covered 9,120 weighted inputs, not an infinite-weight proof. Inputs real signed allowed through absolute value; all n=3,4,5 boundaries covered.
